_doc: STAKEHOLDERS-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-17): who the site is for, what each of them needs, and the path each takes. Source of truth for /for, /for/<id>, /showcase and /showcase/<id> and for the home entry points; site/stakeholders.js is generated from this file by scripts/gen_stakeholders.py and site/site.test.mjs fails if a path step does not resolve, a story is malformed or an audience has no single primary action. To add a domain or a showcase, add a row here; no page code changes. Figures that are estimates say so. No secrets, no unverified claims. Two-domain model (Rowan, 2026-11-17, like WordPress.com and WordPress.org): ultrastable.io is the platform and product for business audiences; ultrastable.org hosts public-benefit demos such as Practical Solutions for data-for-good and AI-for-good audiences. Each demo is a case study on .io and has its own home; /family.json publishes the shared navigation and tokens so a demo renders the same header.

audiences.name: Founders and idea people
audiences.promise: Start with a rough idea. The system works out what to build next and keeps shipping it.
audiences.needs: Direction without code, a clear budget and proof that it is working.

stories.want: to say my idea out loud or in a sentence
stories.so: I do not have to know what to ask for

stories.want: to know if my idea is a fit before anything is built
stories.so: I do not pay for machinery I do not need

stories.want: to see what changed, why and whether it worked
stories.so: I can trust the system without reading code

audiences.name: Nonprofits and communities
audiences.promise: Evidence-based, practical help for good causes and small teams, built in the open and kept current by a system that checks its own sources.
audiences.needs: Plain words, low cost, nothing to install and a way to see that it does good.

stories.want: routine work handled and kept up to date
stories.so: our few people can focus on the cause

stories.want: to see how the practical-help project is doing
stories.so: I can decide whether to help or to use it

stories.want: to know the cost and the limits up front

audiences.name: Developers and engineering teams
audiences.promise: A control loop around the coding agents you already use: it picks the work, proves each change live and reverts regressions.
audiences.needs: Source, an API, agent hooks and an audit trail.

stories.want: to connect my coding agent in one click
stories.so: it takes work from the shared queue

stories.want: an audit trail of every agent change and its prediction
stories.so: I can review decisions, not diffs

stories.want: failed deploys to revert and file their own issue
stories.so: nobody pages me for a known failure

audiences.name: Funders and investors
audiences.promise: One operating system with two live test cases and its own cost and failure record.
audiences.needs: Evidence, status without hype, risks and the licence terms.

stories.want: to see measured results, not claims
stories.so: I can judge the work on evidence

stories.want: the licence and commercial terms plainly stated
stories.so: I know what can and cannot be done with it
I know what stage this is at

audiences.name: Partners and press
audiences.promise: A system that develops itself and its products with one loop. The story, the evidence and a person to ask.
audiences.needs: A short story, citable facts and a contact.

stories.want: a plain explanation with checkable facts
to see where the work fits mine
the decision records and failure history
stories.so: I can study how autonomous systems behave

showcases.name: QNFO
showcases.summary: A large service fleet that Ultrastable ran as customer zero. It exposed real failures, real cost and real limits, then handed the fixes to the platform.
showcases.problem: The audit database read billions of rows a week, mostly from triggers and scans that ran on every tick, and every deploy touched more workers than the change needed.
showcases.loop: The cost loop measured reads per query, traced them to their source, filed the work with a closing probe, and the executor shipped it. Deploys now name the workers they touch and are capped.
results: Audit database daily rows read: 1.37 billion on 11-12, 0.32 billion on 11-16, about 63 million a day over the latest six hours. Part of the drop is a deploy freeze, so "about 95%" is an estimate until the next unfrozen reading.
Worst single query: 2.5 million rows down to under 6,000.
showcases.separate: QNFO is a separate, earlier project and is not Ultrastable. It is no longer in active development; its papers and pages stay online at qnfo.org. It appears here only as the testbed Ultrastable was first proven on.
showcases.learned: Cost is a loop to close like any failure. The fixes now live in the platform, not in QNFO.

showcases.name: Practical Solutions
showcases.summary: A public, evidence-based catalogue of implementable solutions to pressing global problems. Each entry cites a published study and says where it worked, what it takes, who can act and the cheapest first test.
showcases.problem: Lists of the world's problems are long and unranked, and advice on what to do often runs ahead of the evidence.
showcases.loop: Every six hours the loop refreshes the problem ranking from World Bank data. It re-checks the stalest citations, searches for new systematic reviews on the top-ranked problems, quotes their results unchanged and has a separate step verify each quote against the abstract. Every change goes in a public changelog. Leads and bright spots are labelled as leads, never findings.
results: Live public site with problems, solutions, search, changelog, feed and a machine-readable index.
The problem ranking is computed by code from public indicators (shortfall to international targets), not edited by hand.
A solution entry needs a citation, the study's own figures, limits and a cheapest first test; the loop proposes leads but never promotes one on its own.
showcases.learned: A second, unrelated system for data and AI for good runs on the same loop and the same honesty rules as the platform.

showcases.name: Unlearn
showcases.summary: A clickable encyclopedia of popular beliefs the evidence contradicts. Each entry starts from why the belief feels true, asks the reader to guess, then shows graded evidence with named sources.
showcases.problem: Popular beliefs about crime, learning, health, money and policy often run against the research, and being told so rarely changes a mind.
showcases.loop: Every hour the loop resolves each cited study to a DOI through Crossref and searches Europe PMC for new systematic reviews on each entry. New reviews appear on the entry and send it to the re-grading queue. Readers' anonymous guesses and 'did this change your view' taps measure which beliefs surprise and which explanations work, and wording trials keep the explanations that work.
results: Live public site with topics, a play mode, a Lab for candidate beliefs and a machine-readable index.
Every entry cites its sources and is graded by the strength and direction of the evidence; a mixed body of evidence is shown as mixed.
Evidence freshness and the reader shift share are published live at /api/freshness and /api/metrics on the site.
showcases.learned: A third system, unrelated to the first two, runs on the same loop and promotes itself through the same social module as every other tenant.

showcases.name: What Works
showcases.summary: A living atlas of what works in public policy. Each programme is graded from its trials by a published rubric, and readers guess the verdict before they see it.
showcases.problem: Programmes that feel like they should work, such as Scared Straight or D.A.R.E., often did nothing or did harm when they were tested, and the evidence is scattered across journals.
showcases.loop: On its clock the loop resolves cited studies to a DOI through Crossref and searches OpenAlex and Europe PMC for new trials of each programme. A new trial is read in only when a model's labels are backed by quotes copied word for word from its abstract, and then counts at half weight. Every programme is re-graded and each change of verdict is logged with the study that moved it.
results: Live public site with five policy areas, a guess-first page per programme and the rubric shown in full.
Grades come from the trials through the rubric code, and re-grades are published at /changes and in the feed.
Evidence freshness and reader guesses are published live at /api/freshness and /api/metrics on the site.
showcases.learned: A fourth system runs on the same loop, ships from its own repository and promotes itself through the same social module as every other tenant.

showcases.name: Replication Ledger
showcases.summary: A record of which landmark findings held up when others tried to repeat them, and which did not. Readers guess first, then see the attempts.
showcases.problem: Famous findings keep getting taught and cited after attempts to repeat them failed.
showcases.loop: The loop searches OpenAlex and Crossref for new replications, reanalyses and retractions of each finding, files them under a verbatim-quote guard, recomputes the standings with one rubric and logs a move with the paper that moved it.
results: Live public site where each standing comes from the replication attempts on record.
showcases.learned: A fifth system runs on the same loop and evidence guard as Unlearn and What Works.

io.name: Ultrastable
io.role: The platform and product: an autonomous development system that keeps improving what it runs.

org.name: Ultrastable for good
org.role: Public-benefit demos built on the platform, for data-for-good and AI-for-good audiences: free to use, open about method.
